Engineering
Builds

01
Underwater Vehicle for Survey, Search & Rescue
Nov 2023 – Feb 2024 · Bachelor's Thesis, UIU

Engineered a fully functional 6-DOF Remotely Operated Underwater Vehicle (ROUV) from the ground up, designed to assist military search and rescue operations following ferry disasters in Bangladesh.

  • Designed and fine-tuned a YOLO-NAS real-time vision pipeline; validated via mAP, precision, recall, and confusion matrices.
  • Developed an image denoising architecture using DnCNN, significantly improving PSNR and image clarity.
  • Built core control architecture with Raspberry Pi 5 + Pixhawk 4, power/propulsion via ESC units and M080 thrusters, using fiber-optic communication.
  • Custom hydrodynamic frame verified via SolidWorks CFD — withstands up to 3 atmospheres (~30m depth).
  • Algorithmic validation using Gazebo, Blender, and TurtleSim.

Publications

Research
Output

Development of Underwater Vehicle for Survey, Search and Rescue

This research centers on developing and testing a Remotely Operated Underwater Vehicle (ROUV) with a unique 3D design providing six degrees of freedom. The study employs a unique 3D design, hardware implementation, testing, image denoising, and object detection. The ROUV is specifically designed for exploration, search, and rescue missions under water, maintaining fluid dynamics. Inspired by numerous ferry mishaps in Bangladesh to assist the military in overcoming the challenges divers face during rescue incidents. The ROUV is constructed from scratch, selecting hardware-compatible components and improving video footage clarity. It can sustain up to 1.09 atmospheres of pressure and is capable of taking underwater video feeds and storing them.

Authors: Suraia Afroz Maria, Md. Golam Mahmud, Ahmed Junaed Tanim, Md. Yasin, Md. Abid Hossain, Salekul Islam
Venue: 2025 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Communication Engineering (ECCE 2025)
Publisher: IEEE Xplore · 2025
DOI: 10.1109/ECCE64574.2025.11013853
